title: Delhi HC Stays FSSAI Order Barring Dabur's '100%' Claims on Ghee, Honey and Oils
case_name: Dabur India Limited v. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
citation: Delhi High Court, order dated 7 August 2026 (Mahajan, J.)
card_summary: FSSAI's order of 3 August 2026 had directed Dabur to stop selling honey, cow ghee, apple cider vinegar and coconut oil carrying '100%' claims. Justice Amit Mahajan stayed the prohibition, finding it was prima facie passed without a show-cause notice or hearing. The court left open whether the claims mislead consumers, so the stay rests on procedure, not the merits of the labelling objection.
card_tip: A prohibition order under the FSS Act that skips a show-cause notice and hearing is vulnerable to an interim stay regardless of how strong the underlying labelling objection is.
verification_notes: FSSAI order date (3 August 2026), the stay order date (7 August 2026), the bench (Justice Amit Mahajan), the products named (honey, cow ghee, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water and coconut milk), Dabur's no-notice-no-hearing argument, and the court declining to rule on the merits are corroborated across Bar and Bench, Verdictum and The Week. The next hearing was reported as 24 August 2026; no outcome of that hearing was found in available sources, so none is stated.
